title: Servicing Guide: Opening a Property Charge Advance Repayment Record and the One-Record Limit
content:
**Rule.** A loan carries at most the product's maximum number of open arrangement records, and a borrower has only one reverse mortgage, so a borrower holds at most 1 open Property Charge Advance Repayment record. An arrangement record is opened only when the loan has no other record whose status is notice period, pending signature, active or defaulted. While a record is open, every new advance on the loan is added to it rather than opening another. A record opens on the first unrepaid advance, as the product's opening term provides, for any loan program the product covers, under the Lump-Sum Repayment notice, which asks for repayment in full within the product's lump-sum repayment period in calendar days; notices go by the product's notice channels.

## What counts as an open record

| Status of an existing record on the same loan | Is it an open record that bars a new one? |
|---|---|
| Notice period | Yes |
| Pending signature | Yes |
| Active | Yes |
| Defaulted | Yes |
| Completed | Not listed among the open statuses |
| Referred | Not listed among the open statuses |

## Basis of the judgement

- **Evidence.** Whether another open record exists is read from the system's records for the loan — the record's HECM loan or Cedarline Summit loan and its status — before a record is opened; a caller's account of the loan's history does not replace them.
- **Object.** The comparison is made loan by loan: a record bars a new one only when it sits on the same HECM loan or the same Cedarline Summit loan.
- **Limit per borrower.** At most 1 open record per borrower follows from the one-record-per-loan limit together with a borrower holding one reverse mortgage.

## What a newly opened record looks like

A new record opens under the Lump-Sum Repayment arrangement, in the notice period, dated the day of the first advance, and on the HECM loan or the Cedarline Summit loan to which that advance was made.

### Hypothetical cases

| Hypothetical situation on one loan | Outcome under the rule |
|---|---|
| No earlier record; a first property tax advance is made | A record opens under the Lump-Sum Repayment notice |
| A record in active status exists; a further insurance advance is made | No new record opens; the advance is added to the active record |
| A record in defaulted status exists; a further advance is made | No new record opens; the advance is added to the defaulted record |

The situations are illustrations, not borrower facts.
